title: A gap-fill on the independent step
statement: Whether the independent step should give everyone a gap-fill frame, or offer it only after a first miss so it stays no easier than guided practice, is untested.
detail: Curriculum feedback on a Grade 3 reading lesson asked for a gap-fill frame at the last step of the independent turn. The course team pushed back that this would make the independent turn less demanding than the guided turn, whose last step is already a gap-fill, inverting the release gradient, and proposed the gap-fill as a fallback after a first miss so the scaffold is available rather than imposed. A later course record shows the gap-fill built as modelled after an instruction to make every requested change, so the outcome was a ruling, not evidence of what helps learners.

evidence.quote: A gap-fill at step 4 makes the you-do less demanding than the we-do's step 4, which is already a gap-fill — that inverts the release gradient (D1.15) and breaks same-skill-faded (D1.4). Our recommendation is the fallback-after-a-miss version in draft (h)4.
make the gap-fill the *fallback after a first miss*, so the scaffold is available rather than imposed.
Step 4 gap fill as has been modelled (#31).
Make all the changes they have requested - no exceptions
